thread:
sam_support: FYI Aurelia reported that objects they deleted 48+ hours ago are still showing in search results. Legal wants a strict timeline. Details below.
eli_ops: Can you paste the customer ID + an example object id?
sam_support: Cust: aurelia-1432, obj id: obj_6f9a2c. Repro steps they gave:
```
1) DELETE /v1/objects/obj_6f9a2c -> 202 { job_id: jd_983 }
2) GET /v1/search?q=obj_6f9a2c -> returns hit with last_seen: 2026-03-12T09:12:33Z
```
sam_support: They said TTL policy is default 90 days but previously set custom-retention=30d on some namespaces; this particular object was supposed to be expired by the customer's custom TTL on 2026-03-10.
eli_ops: Noted. We rotated a customer-specific KMS key for some accounts yesterday in the 09:00 deploy window. @amy_sre could the rotate have affected tombstone processing?
amy_sre: Possible. Tombstone worker writes tombstone metadata then storage layer re-encrypts indexes; if decrypt fails during index purge we can leave visibility intact. Need logs for jd_983 and tombstone worker between 2026-03-10T00:00-2026-03-12T12:00 UTC.
sam_support: Pasting minimal logs from customer-facing ops (redacted):
```
[2026-03-10T09:01:12Z] DELETE obj_6f9a2c -> job jd_983 accepted
[2026-03-10T09:01:15Z] tombstone-writer: tombstone written obj_6f9a2c key_id=kms-customer-87
[2026-03-10T09:01:17Z] index-purger: reencrypt failed for obj_6f9a2c error=KMS:DecryptDenied
[2026-03-10T09:01:17Z] audit-log: write event tombstone_created job=jd_983
```
eli_ops: index-purger failing decrypt explains visibility retention. KMS returned DecryptDenied. Was that the rotation window?
amy_sre: Yes, rotation for kms-customer-87 started at 2026-03-10T09:00 and completed ~09:05. We need to confirm whether re-encrypt attempted with the new key and lacked permissions.
maria_legal: Legal requests we preserve all current state for Aurelia. Do NOT purge anything that could be relevant until we provide an export and timeline. Put a litigation hold flag on aurelia-1432.
sam_support: On it. Opening hold now. ticketbot: Created ticket SUP-2026-314 and set severity=P1.
deploy-bot: deploy: infra/delete-worker v2.3.4 rolled at 1765555600 to prod (namespace: default, region: us-west-2).
eli_ops: Next steps: 1) Confirm KMS key policy for new key includes service principal used by index-purger. 2) Replay or re-run index-purger for jd_983 in read-only repro mode to validate decrypt. 3) If decrypt permission missing, coordinate with infra-kms to grant decrypt and re-encrypt index entries. 4) Generate export of affected objects and audit logs for legal.
amy_sre: Commands I'll run (internal):
```
# list tombstones
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN" "https://infra.internal/api/tombstones?cust=aurelia-1432&job=jd_983"
# check key usage
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id kms-customer-87
# run index purge dry-run
/opt/infra/bin/index-purger --job jd_983 --dry-run --log-level debug
```
eli_ops: Assigning infra contact @eli_ops -> infra-kms alias to make policy change if confirmed. Also tagging eng-sre to monitor re-encrypt job.
maria_legal: For the export please include: object payloads (redacted where required), tombstone metadata, audit-log entries for delete/tombstone events, and KMS key rotation timeline. We need a signed checksum and chain-of-custody note.
sam_support: Notified customer that we're preserving data and initiated SUP-2026-314. They'll expect ETA for export + a patch.
amy_sre: I'm seeing a batch of ~123 objects for aurelia-1432 that had index-purger decrypt failures between 09:00-09:06. I'll attempt policy check first. If we can fix policy, we can re-run re-encrypt and then purge; otherwise we will provide full export and work with legal on retention exception.
eli_ops: If re-encrypt succeeds, do NOT auto-purge until legal says ok. Mark ticket with action_required:infra-kms,action_required:eng-sre, preserve_until=legal_release.
sam_support: I'll keep customer updated and request any additional object ids they want included. Will report back in this thread within 2 hours. :thumbsup:
